newsitem.title: FRANCE: ROWING-REDGRAVE, PINSENT MAKE IT 66 WINS IN A ROW.
newsitem.headline: ROWING-REDGRAVE, PINSENT MAKE IT 66 WINS IN A ROW.

text.p: Quadruple Olympic gold medallist Steve Redgrave and Matthew Pinsent extended their unbeaten record to 66 victories on Sunday at the rowing World Cup.
Redgrave and Pinsent, with fellow Britons Tim Foster and James Cracknell, won the coxless fours in five minutes 48.16 seconds ahead of runners-up France in 5:48.93.
Germany took the Paris regatta title with 59 points to extend their overall tally after two World Cup events to 139 points. Britain were second here on 39 points for 73 overall.

Redgrave's and Pisent's unbeaten record started in May 1992 and comprises 61 successive wins in the coxless pairs and five in the coxless four, three at the opening World Cup regatta in Munich three weeks ago.

The British quartet were pushed all the way in the final by a new French crew, including three former world champions in Jean-Christophe Rolland, Michel Andrieux and Daniel Fauche, now rowing with Gilles Bosquet.
Britain's four got the better start but the crews were virtually level at the 750-metrem mark, then Pinsent at stroke put in another burst and the British moved ahead by halfway.
In their final burst, Pinsent caught a crab but the British maintained their lead to cross the line a canvas ahead of their rivals.

Double Olympic gold medallist Pinsent said: "It was a close race but we were never worried. My blade caught a crab and went in on the feather. I've caught two now -- I did one in Munich. I owe the boys two."
French strokeman Jean-Christophe Rolland said: "The conditions here were very difficult. In normal conditions we can get closer to them. We don't think they are unbeatable."
Despite the difficult conditions, the lightweight coxless four from Denmark set a world record of 5:51.54, beating the previous mark of 5:52.34 set by Italy at Lucerne in 1995.
In the men's single sculls, Slovenia's former world champion Iztok Cop made it two World Cup wins in a row, again defeating Egypt's Ibrahim Ali, the new discovery of the season.
